title: Native Local Split Scanned Book
script: Welcome to this deep dive into Native Local Split Scanned Book. Part of PaperPilot's native Document Operations suite, this tool provides deterministic, local-first execution. Engineered entirely in pure Rust, it operates with zero cloud egress, giving you complete data privacy, no SaaS subscription fees, and no external API rate limits. Now let us examine the input parameters and what each signifies. You configure input, an required parameter for Path to the input PDF containing double-page scans.. In addition, reading_direction, an optional parameter for Reading order of halves: 'ltr' (left-then-right) or 'rtl' (right-then-left).. In addition, gutter_overlap, an optional parameter for Optional center gutter overlap margin in PDF points.. In addition, split_horizontal, an optional parameter for Split top/bottom horizontally instead of left/right vertically.. Every parameter is rigorously validated in memory before processing begins, ensuring safe, predictable transformations across all your documents. Next, output files and metrics. The tool emits optimized .pdf documents at Destination path for the split single-page .pdf file.. By pruning redundant objects, deduplicating font streams, and applying memory-safe Rayon parallelism, it slashes document file size by up to eighty percent in under fifteen milliseconds, with zero bytes leaked to the cloud. You can deploy pdf_split_scanned_book across all five universal interfaces. First, drag and drop in the desktop dock for live inspection. Second, call it autonomously from Claude or AI agents through our native Model Context Protocol server. Third, run it directly in your terminal with the PaperPilot CLI. Fourth, trigger it via local REST API POST requests at localhost port 8080. And fifth, execute it client-side in your browser with zero-upload WebAssembly. Unlock total document privacy and native performance today. Visit usepaperpilot.com to explore pdf_split_scanned_book and all one hundred tools, run live interactive benchmarks, and download the bare-metal binary. Local-first document intelligence, powered by PaperPilot.
